note: The peer certificate bytes arrive from the network handshake and are parsed in-place without copying when peer certificate retention is disabled.

note: The nocopy wrapper forwards the attacker-controlled buffer into the core parser with make_copy=0, so the certificate object will alias the handshake buffer.
The parsed certificate stores a raw pointer into the handshake message instead of allocating its own copy.
If any later ASN.1 field fails to parse, the partially initialized certificate is freed while still containing aliases into the handshake buffer.

code: crt_start = chain->raw.p; crt_len = chain->raw.len; ... mbedtls_x509_crt_free( chain ); mbedtls_free( chain );
note: The TLS layer later snapshots pointers into the certificate raw bytes and then frees the certificate object, leaving those saved pointers dependent on freed storage.
The saved pointer is dereferenced to hash the peer certificate after the certificate object has been freed, which is the memory-safety sink that can read freed bytes and crash under ASAN.
